Model-based projection and light quantifier elimination

Source: R/models.R
z3_model_project.Rd

Spacer's utilities for eliminating variables from a formula.

Usage

z3_model_project(
  model,
  vars,
  formula,
  method = c("plain", "witness", "skolem")
)

z3_model_extrapolate(model, formula)

z3_qe_lite(vars, formula)

Arguments

model

A z3_model.

vars

A constant or a list of constants.

formula

A Boolean expression.

method

"plain", "witness" or "skolem".

Value

An expression, or a list as described above.

Details

  • z3_model_project(model, vars, formula) performs model-based projection: it returns a formula free of vars that is true in model and implies exists vars. formula. formula must be true in model (an error otherwise). Variables Z3 cannot eliminate, such as some arrays, stay in the result. With method = "witness" (Z3 4.13.4) the result is a list with the projected formula and, in vars and terms, terms for the eliminated variables that keep the formula true in the model when substituted for them; with method = "skolem", the list holds the Skolem terms recorded by arithmetic projection.

  • z3_model_extrapolate(model, formula) returns a conjunction of literals that is true in model and implies formula (an implicant of formula taken from the model); formula must be true in model.

  • z3_qe_lite(vars, formula) eliminates, where it is cheap to do so, the variables vars from exists vars. formula. It returns a list with the result formula and the variables that remaining free in it.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")
f <- x > 2 & y == x + 1
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, f)
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
m <- z3_model(sol)
z3_model_project(m, x, f)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (not (<= y 3))
z3_model_extrapolate(m, f | y < 0)
#> <z3_expr Bool> (and (= y (+ x 1)) (> x 2))
z3_qe_lite(x, y == x + 1 & x > 2)
#> $formula
#> <z3_expr Bool> (> (+ (- 1) y) 2)
#> 
#> $remaining
#> list()
#>
